content.comment_body: Hello. Can I connect [product_name] 24V expansion modules to a [product_name] 230V base module? Thanks for any advice.

You can't directly connect a 24V expansion module after a 230V base module, but there is a workaround: Placing an analog module between the 230V base module and the 24V expansion modules enables this setup.

That's correct, and the manufacturer even recommends this if the PV input of a controller is used (see [document]). However, people may avoid buying an expensive module if they don't actually need it. Plus, this approach can negatively affect fast communication with downstream digital modules.

Understood, but if an application requires both 230V and 24V modules, using an extra analog module is likely more cost-effective than buying two base modules. Managing two base modules also means handling two user programs, so I'd prefer a single-module solution.
Actually, you don't need two programs. With master/slave communication, only the master module is programmed.

analysis.insight_summary: Users discussed how to connect 24V digital expansion modules to a 230V base module. The main issue is that modules with different voltage requirements aren't compatible directly, leading to recommendations for using additional analog modules or master/slave communication between multiple base modules. Trade-offs between simplicity, cost, communication speed, and total module count were central to the conversation.
analysis.user_expectations: Users hope to add 24V digital modules to a 230V base module in a straightforward, easy manner. They seek confirmation of possible compatibility and simple solutions that avoid complex workarounds.
